root_cause.text: `nf_conntrack_helper_unregister()` in the netfilter conntrack helper subsystem passed `NULL` to `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy()`, so the cleanup callback `expect_iter_me()` never matched and removed expectations tied to the helper, leaving dangling `exp->helper` references after the helper object was freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, NULL);` to `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, me);`, and the CVE text states that passing `NULL` caused “all of them survive the cleanup,” after which `nfnl_cthelper_del()` frees the helper and later expectation dumps or `init_conntrack()` dereference freed `exp->helper`, producing a use-after-free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the unregistering helper into expectation cleanup so its related expectations are destroyed correctly.
intent_record.what: In nf_conntrack_helper_unregister(), the second argument passed to nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy() was changed from NULL to me, while the surrounding code remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the expectation-iteration destroy callback now receives the helper being unregistered instead of a null pointer, allowing the destroy logic to operate specifically on that helper's expectations rather than using a non-specific or no-op context.

candidates.rationale: This call passes NULL to the expectation-destruction iterator, so the cleanup callback cannot match expectations belonging to the unregistering helper. As a result, helper-linked expectations remain allocated and later dangle after the helper is freed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call passes NULL instead of the unregistering helper to the expectation cleanup iterator, so expect_iter_me() cannot match and remove expectations associated with that helper. Those expectations remain linked to a freed helper, creating dangling exp->helper references.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body already contains the corrected cleanup path. In the old code, expectations were explicitly walked under `spin_lock_bh(&nf_conntrack_expect_lock)` and removed when either `help->helper == me` or `exp->helper == me`. In this commit, that open-coded loop is replaced by `nf_ct_expect_iterate_destroy(expect_iter_me, NULL);`, and the new callback `expect_iter_me()` clearly matches both cases: `if (exp->helper == me) return true;` and `return this == me;`. This means the vulnerable construct described in the root cause—passing `NULL` so that the cleanup callback never matched—is not present here; the helper unregister path now uses the matching iterator callback to remove the expectations.
